clues: This city sits on the Black Sea coast of a peninsula. A long road runs through it and links shore towns on each side.
The mountains near this town help make its land arid and rocky. Dry ground, not rich green fields, marks the shore here.
In the 1400s, men from Genoa built a strong fort here. In their years of rule, they changed the town's name to a shorter form.
Adam Mickiewicz, a famed poet, gave this place two of his sonnets. His Crimean Sonnets still link his name to this shore town.
Stone bits still stand from an old Byzantine tower, part of a fort that gave this town its name. Seek that tower by the shore.
